subject: Private connectivity assessment — BlueHarbor: hosting path & allowlist next steps
messages:
From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
To: Alex Green <alex.green@blueharbor.com>; Sara Li <sara.li@blueharbor.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>; Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-07-28T15:12:00-07:00
Subject: Quick follow-up + checklist (Private VPC path)

Alex / Sara — thanks again for the call today. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we have alignment across teams.

Recap
- BlueHarbor preference: evaluate Private VPC (isolation + control) vs Dedicated capacity for predictable throughput. During the call you indicated Private VPC is the leading option.
- Primary concerns you raised: PrivateLink vs VPC Peering, egress ownership (who provides egress IPs), and minimal allowlist surface for your firewall team.

What I can action this week
1) Share our Private VPC networking checklist (attached) and a short matrix that contrasts PrivateLink vs Peering for common patterns.
2) Pull the current egress IP ranges we publish for PrivateLink endpoints and typical Dedicated egress blocks so you can share with NetOps.
3) Provide SOC2/attestation pointer for procurement.

Asks from your side
- Can your NetOps team confirm whether they require a fixed set of IPv4 prefixes (CIDRs) or if they can accept FQDN-based allowlisting for outbound connections?
- If PrivateLink: will BlueHarbor manage NAT/eBGP on your side or would you prefer Redwood to provide fixed egress IPs?
- Suggested 30-min follow-up with NetOps + SecOps to lock down ports/egress model — any availability Tuesday or Wednesday next week?

I've attached the checklist and a CSV with the ports we commonly ask customers to open for PrivateLink/peering flows. If helpful I can convert to a one-page diff for your firewall team.

-Jonas
Jonas Weber
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
jonas.weber@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0192

Attachments: redwood_private_vpc_checklist.pdf (7 pages); blueharbor_network_ports.csv

From: Alex Green <alex.green@blueharbor.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
Cc: Sara Li <sara.li@blueharbor.com>; network@blueharbor.com
Date: 2028-07-28T18:04:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Quick follow-up + checklist (Private VPC path)

Jonas — thanks, this is perfect. Short answers for your asks and a couple of clarifying questions from NetOps.

NetOps note (cc'd): we prefer a minimal CIDR allowlist where possible, but for some managed services we can accept FQDN allowlisting as a fallback. Primary requirement is that any IPs you provide for our egress allowlist must be stable for at least 90 days or we need a change window.

PrivateLink vs Peering
- We lean toward PrivateLink for cross-account endpoint isolation, but if PrivateLink introduces many endpoints / more complicated DNS we may examine peering. Can you confirm whether Redwood requires outbound connections from our VPC to your control plane during PrivateLink setup and whether those endpoints have stable FQDNs?

Egress ownership
- BlueHarbor prefers to own egress where possible (we manage NAT and egress firewall). If Redwood needs stable egress IPs for features like model telemetry or observability callbacks, we can accept a small set of IPs to be allowlisted.

Procurement / Security
- Please attach SOC2 type II report or a link to the attestation; procurement will need that for the sourcing doc.

Timing
- NetOps is available Tue 2028-07-31 10:00–10:30 PT or Wed 2028-08-01 14:00–14:30 PT for a short sync. Which works for you?

Thanks,
Alex
Alex Green
Platform Engineering Manager — BlueHarbor Capital
alex.green@blueharbor.com

From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>; Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
Cc: Alex Green <alex.green@blueharbor.com>; Sara Li <sara.li@blueharbor.com>
Date: 2028-07-29T09:22:00-07:00
Subject: Fwd: Quick follow-up + checklist (Private VPC path) — NetOps asks (PrivateLink egress + SOC2)

Marissa / Neha — forwarding BlueHarbor's notes. They prefer PrivateLink but want clarity on:
- Do we require BlueHarbor to open outbound connections to our control plane during provisioning? If yes, what FQDNs/IPs and are any of those source-IP-specific?
- Can we provide a 90-day-stable egress IP set for telemetry/callbacks if BlueHarbor wants to own NAT?
- Please attach SOC2 type II link for procurement (they asked specifically).

Goal: confirm the minimal allowlist we can give them this week and lock a 30-min netops sync for Tue 7/31 10:00 PT. If one of you can own the call, I'll send calendar invite and invite BlueHarbor's network@ address.

Thanks — Jonas

From: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>; Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-07-29T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Quick follow-up + checklist (Private VPC path) — NetOps asks (PrivateLink egress + SOC2)

Quick answers from security:
- SOC2 type II: link (internal): https://redwood-secure.company/soc2/typeii/2027 — I'll export a procurement-ready PDF and attach to the invite.
- PrivateLink provisioning: provisioning control plane calls (account verification, endpoint state) require outbound connections to our control plane on port 443 to api.redwood.com. We publish stable FQDNs; we can provide a short list of CNAMEs and the current egress IP ranges used by our edge control plane. We cannot guarantee IP stability for all control plane hosts beyond 90 days due to cloud routing, but will commit to providing a change window and notification.
- Telemetry callbacks: we offer optional fixed egress IP blocks for customers on PrivateLink — we can allocate an up-to-4-IP set for observability callbacks if BlueHarbor wants allowlisting, otherwise they can keep NAT on their side and we'll use FQDN-based endpoints.

I'll prepare the small IP set and the procurement SOC2 PDF by EOD Monday. Marissa — can you own the ops invite and share dial-in notes?

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Alex Green <alex.green@blueharbor.com>; network@blueharbor.com
Cc: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>; Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-07-30T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Quick follow-up + checklist (Private VPC path) — NetOps sync invite

Alex / NetOps — thanks for the signal. Jonas and I will join Tue 2028-07-31 10:00 PT. Call agenda (15–20 min):
1) Confirm allowlist model (CIDR vs FQDN) and agree change window for any IP updates.
2) Share the 4-IP telemetry block (if BlueHarbor wants fixed egress) and the control-plane FQDNs we use for provisioning.
3) Clarify port list (attached CSV) and inbound peering requirements if you decide peering instead of PrivateLink.

I'll attach the SOC2 PDF and the small IP block in the invite. Please send any firewall contact directly to network@blueharbor.com so we can include them on the invite.

Invite sent — calendar attached. Looking forward to the sync.

-Marissa
Marissa Cole
Customer Success Manager, Redwood Inference
